question: Is the magnitude of lineage-specific trait-allocation deviation a repeatable family property across disjoint trait subsets, and does that propensity transfer between BIEN and AusTraits?

allocation_amplitude.trait_residual: rho_ft minus the source-wide mean rho of trait t
allocation_amplitude.family_subset_centering: within each family and trait subset subtract the family mean residual, removing lineage-wide memory level
allocation_amplitude.amplitude: RMS of the centered trait residuals

within_source_repeatability.partition: enumerate balanced disjoint trait partitions; BIEN 6+6, AusTraits 6+7
within_source_repeatability.family_requirement: at least 2 observed traits in each half
within_source_repeatability.statistic: Spearman correlation across families between half-A and half-B allocation amplitudes
within_source_repeatability.support_adjustment: also residualize each half amplitude on number of observed traits in that half and mean log species support before correlation

cross_source_transfer.population: families shared by BIEN and AusTraits
cross_source_transfer.statistic: Spearman correlation of full-trait allocation amplitude
cross_source_transfer.adjustment: also compare residual amplitudes after source-specific adjustment for observed trait count and mean log species support; BIEN additionally adjusts mean rho SE

interpretation.within_source_positive_cross_source_null: allocation amplitude is structured within a given trait universe but is not a universal family scalar; it depends on lineage x trait-domain context
interpretation.within_and_cross_positive: some lineages possess a transferable rewiring propensity
interpretation.within_null: allocation amplitude is primarily trait-pair-specific rather than family-level
